extracted.intended_audience: Individuals, organizations, and stakeholders submitting public comments to the HHS Office for Civil Rights on this NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on an HHS Office for Civil Rights notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM), including acceptable submission methods, format preferences, docket identification, and posting/redaction policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (comment deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period for the NPRM ... is re-opened. Comments should be received on or before February 20, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments submitted or postmarked after the due date will not be accepted. Allow sufficient time for mailed comments to be timely received in the event of delivery or security delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments, identified by agency name and Docket No. OCR-2026-0034, by any of the following methods: Electronic Submissions via the Federal eRulemaking Portal (https://www.regulations.gov) or Written Submissions by mail to the specified HHS address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions on Regulations.gov for electronic submissions. Do not submit comments by fax or email; such submissions will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and searchable-text preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department strongly encourages you to submit any comments or attachments in Microsoft Word format. If you must submit a comment in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF), the Department strongly encourages you to convert the PDF to 'print-to-PDF' format, or to use some other commonly used searchable text format. Please do not submit the PDF in scanned format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a print-to-PDF or other searchable format allows the Department to electronically search and copy portions of submissions to assist in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket identification in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be identified by agency name and Docket No. OCR-2026-0034 so they are filed in the correct docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the docket number on electronic or mailed submissions to ensure placement and retrieval in the proper administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and availability of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received by the methods and due date specified will be posted without change to https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided, and such posting may occur after the closing of the comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume private submissions; anything included may become publicly viewable unless redacted by the Department under its redaction policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction policy and examples of redactable content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may redact certain non-substantive content from comments before posting, including threats, hate speech, profanity, graphic images, or individually identifiable information about an individual third-party other than the commenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that portions of submissions may be removed prior to posting; avoid including non-substantive or sensitive third-party personal information if you want content to remain public and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality/designation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments or material designated as confidential or not to be disclosed to the public will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not label submissions as confidential with the expectation they will be withheld; such designations are not accepted and the Department will not process them as confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of redaction or rejection on rulemaking consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not consider in rulemaking any redacted or rejected content that would not be made available to the public as part of the administrative record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantive material is removed or rejected and thus not part of the public record, it will not be considered in the agency's rulemaking deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail submission instructions and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail written submissions to: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights, Attention: Disability NPRM, RIN 0945-AA27, Hubert H. Humphrey Building, Room 509F, 200 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow sufficient time for mailed comments to be timely received, taking into account delivery and security delays; ensure mail is postmarked by the due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing docket and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to https://www.regulations.gov and follow the instructions provided for conducting a search, using the docket number(s) found in the heading of this document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the docket number OCR-2026-0034 on Regulations.gov to locate supporting documents and comments for this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement / receipt policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the large number of public comments normally received on Federal Register documents, the Office for Civil Rights is not able to provide individual acknowledgements of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect an individual confirmation of receipt; check Regulations.gov docket for posting status instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for further information
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information contact John Thompson, Office for Civil Rights, Department of Health and Human Services at (202) 545-4884 or (800) 537-7697 (TDD), or via email at 504@hhs.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contact information for procedural or informational questions about the NPRM or comment process.
